title: South Korea's top court overturns charges against ex-prime minister for his role in martial law
summary: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned the conviction of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo for aiding in the declaration of martial law in December 2024.

image.caption: FILE - Former South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, center, arrives at the Seoul Central District Court for his first sentencing trial in the insurrection case, in Seoul, South Korea, Jan. 21, 2026. (Chung Sung-Jun via The Associated Press)

blocks.text: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned the conviction of former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo for aiding in the declaration of martial law in December 2024.
The court ruled that prosecutors had not sufficiently proven the case
Han was convicted for aiding ousted president Yoon Suk Yeol in legitimizing the decree by securing its endorsement at a Cabinet meeting.

items: South Korea's ex-president Yoon receives life sentence for imposing martial law

blocks.text: The court on Thursday ruled that prosecutors had not sufficiently proven the case.
Han's case will now be sent back to the Seoul High Court, which sentenced him to 15 years in prison in May.
But the Supreme Court upheld a four-year prison term for Yoon's wife, Kim Keon Hee, on corruption charges, including stock price manipulation and bribery.
Han and Kim, both currently imprisoned, did not attend the ruling.
